claims.text: Thermal activation near the melting regime promotes atomic-scale chemical short-range ordering in Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles.
Chemical short-range ordering causes local clustering of lower-melting constituents.
Chemically enriched zones depress the local melting temperature.
The enriched zones broaden the overall premelting and melting transitions.
The enriched zones shift the overall premelting and melting transitions relative to particles with minimal short-range order.
The initial equiatomic Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles are solid solutions with minimal pre-existing internal chemical ordering.
Annealing near 0.9 times the bulk melting temperature permits atomic rearrangement without complete melting.
The thermally generated clusters are enriched in Cu and Co, which are identified as lower-melting constituents.
Differences in bonding strengths among the constituent elements drive preferential atomic pairing during thermal annealing.
Preferential atomic pairing produces nanoscale short-range order and aggregation of lower-melting elements into clusters.
Lower-melting-element clusters act as premelting nucleation sites by lowering the local melting barrier.
Longer sub-melting dwell times produce greater short-range order and more advanced element-specific clustering than shorter dwell times.
Greater short-range order from longer dwell times decreases the premelting onset temperature.
Greater short-range order from longer dwell times broadens the melting transition profile.
Particles receiving minimal thermal dwell exhibit minimal short-range order.
Particles with minimal short-range order have melting behavior closer to an ideal random solid solution and a sharper transition.
